text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected on canary group 'v5-canary' in us-west for streaming endpoints. p99 = 2.8s (SLO 1.2s). Auto-notify on-call.

alex_oncall: acked. I’m looking. paging now. :pager:

jordan_sre: seeing same in graphs — sudden p99 jump at 09:13 UTC. p95 up to 1.1s, p99 2.8s. tail shape skewed on streaming (chunked responses).

priya_runtime: can confirm rollout yesterday shifted 20% traffic to v5-canary with new KV cache change & quant kernel tweak. Any errors?

jordan_sre: error rate steady, no obvious 5xx spike. logs show repeated resend/retry between inference workers and multiplexer:

```
2026-03-14T09:13:21Z mux.go:412 warn: chunk send stalled for 350ms -> retry
2026-03-14T09:13:22Z worker-7: kvcache miss, fallback to slow path (50ms)
2026-03-14T09:13:23Z streaming: token flush delayed 420ms
```

luis_support: customer telemetry (top 50 apps) shows ~1.2% of requests timed out at client side in last 15m; highest for streaming chat flows. Not yet any support tickets but slack mentions increased latencies.

kate_pm: quick ask: do we have rollback playbook for canary traffic shift? need ETA for mitigation and note for customer comms.

priya_runtime: options: 1) immediate rollback of canary weight to 0 (route-level change) 2) divert streaming endpoints off canary 3) throttle canary traffic. Rollback safe? config pinned to v4 available.

alex_oncall: prefer traffic divert + quick rollback if divert doesn't help. Can someone run route adjust and scale a small hotfix to mux?

priya_runtime: running routing change now: `infractl route adjust --service=canary-router --weight=v5-canary=0 --reason="p99 spike"`

deploy-bot: starting route update job ID 8912. Estimated propagation 30s.

jordan_sre: while that propagates, I'm enabling increased worker timeout logging and turning on aggressive KV cache warm-up for v4 to reduce cold misses: `srectl feature toggle kv-warmup --env=canary --enable`

incident-bot: Route update job 8912: SUCCESS at 09:14:05 UTC. v5-canary weight = 0.

luis_support: metrics after route change (09:14–09:20): p99 dropped to 1.5s, p95 0.95s. Client timedouts down to 0.2% in latest 5m.

priya_runtime: looks like routing rollback reduced tail. I recommend holding v5 at 0 and pausing rollout. We should capture traces for the offending model variant and run a small replay.

jordan_sre: agree. Opening a follow-up incident for post-mortem: increased sampling on streaming traces and collect kvcache miss histograms for v5.

kate_pm: we’ll prepare a short customer note: summary + "no ongoing impact" once we validate. Kate to draft, Luis to review.

alex_oncall: handing off to priya_runtime for live mitigation and post-mortem runbook. I’m stepping out for the next 25m but available by DM if needed. :white_check_mark:

priya_runtime: taking over. Next actions: 1) keep v5 weight=0 2) run `replay --model=v5-canary --subset=100k` on staging traces 3) compare kernel perf and kv miss patterns vs v4 4) meet SRE in 30m for findings.

jordan_sre: noted. Added paging to oncall rotation for deeper dive. If we see p99 > 1.5s again, escalate to platform lead.

luis_support: will watch customer channels and queue; prepping comms. Will post draft in #customer-updates.

priya_runtime: quick dump of next-step command snippets that we used:

```
infractl route adjust --service=canary-router --weight=v5-canary=0 --who=priya
srectl feature toggle kv-warmup --env=canary --enable
tracectl sample --service=streaming --model=v5-canary --rate=100%
```

priya_runtime: creating a post-mortem ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + sre. tagging as P2; will include timeline and mitigation commands.

incident-bot: incident closed (mitigation applied) at 09:20:00 UTC — severity reduced to monitoring.

kate_pm: thanks all — good coordination. Follow-up sync in 30m in #incidents-postmortem.

priya_runtime: will capture perf diffs and upload profile artifacts to the ticket.

alex_oncall: thanks team. :thumbsup:
